\begin{lemma}[Binary width bound from a configuration code]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.width_of_code}
\label{Complexity.Codec.width_of_code}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x,y$ be finite bit strings, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $C$ be a
configuration of a finite-tape Turing machine on input $x$. If the configuration word
for $C$ with window parameter $s$ has length at most $|y|$, then the length of the
binary expansion of $s$ is at most the length of the binary expansion of $|y|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Configuration word length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_le_length}
\label{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_le_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgWord, Turing.Cfg, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$
be a Boolean input word, let $C$ be a configuration of $N$ on input $x$, and let
$s\in\mathbb{N}$. For every Boolean list $r$, the length of the encoded configuration
word is at most the length of the pair encoding of $x$ with the pair encoding of that
configuration word and $r$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Preliminary certificate check]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.PreChk}
\label{Complexity.Codec.PreChk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ and $w$ be a finite Boolean string. The predicate holds exactly when
$w$ has length $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(n)+1$, its bit at position $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(n)$ (using
`false` if that position is out of range) is true, and the natural number encoded by the
length-$w_P(n)$ segment of $w$ beginning at position $W(N)(2s+1)$ is at most $n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Validity Check and Its Preliminary Conditions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre}
\label{Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.PreChk, Complexity.Codec.VAcc, Complexity.Codec.ValidChk, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.vScan}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb N$ and $w$ be a finite Boolean word. The validity condition on $w$ is
equivalent to the conjunction of the following preliminary conditions and the verifier
acceptance test on the prefix of length $W(2s+1)$: $|w|=W(2s+1)+wP(n)+1$, the bit of $w$
at position $W(2s+1)+wP(n)$ is true, and the integer represented by the $wP(n)$ bits
immediately after the first $W(2s+1)$ bits, read with the first bit least significant,
is at most $n+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Initial execution of the codec program]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.one_run}
\label{Complexity.Codec.one_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.CA, Complexity.Codec.PreChk, Complexity.Codec.Reach, Complexity.Codec.Reach.trans, Complexity.Codec.Regs, Complexity.Codec.Regs.Bd, Complexity.Codec.Regs.val, Complexity.Codec.Shape1, Complexity.Codec.VAd, Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow, Complexity.Codec.bnd, Complexity.Codec.bnd_ge, Complexity.Codec.layR, Complexity.Codec.layout_run, Complexity.Codec.le_phase, Complexity.Codec.orc, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.parse_run, Complexity.Codec.s_le_of_width, Complexity.LogProg.two_pow_bits_le, Complexity.Codec.vScan, Complexity.Codec.vscan_run, Complexity.Codec.wP, Complexity.Codec.wP_le, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.length_pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let
$\mathrm{mode}$ be one of the codec modes other than the step mode. For every bit string
$y$, at least one of the following holds. Either there are bit strings $x,w$ and a
natural number $s$ such that $y=\langle x,\langle w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$,
$|\mathrm{bits}(s)|\leq |\mathrm{bits}(|y|)|$, and, writing $W$ for the chunk width, $w$
has length $W(2s+1)+|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|+1$, has a $1$ at position
$W(2s+1)+|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|$, and the value of the following $|\mathrm{bits}(|x|)|$
bits is at most $|x|+1$; moreover there are a scan state $st$ and register values $R$
such that $st$ is the scan of the first $W(2s+1)$ bits of $w$, every register of $R$ is
at most $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, and $R_A=2|x|+2$, $R_S=s$, $R_T=0$, and $R_{Pos}$ is the value
of those following bits. The codec register program, started at its length-scan label
with all registers zero and run with its two membership oracles on input $y$, can reach
its completion label with state $st$ and registers $R$, while throughout the run its
configuration satisfies the program’s precondition and every register remains at most
$(8W+8)(|y|+1)$. Or else every representation $y=\langle x,\langle
w,\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ satisfying the stated bit-length bound fails the
stated length, marker-bit, or payload-value checks, and the same program, from the same
initial configuration and under the same register bound and precondition, halts with
answer false.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Syntactic conditions on edge-tail instructions]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.EdgeOK}
\label{Complexity.Codec.EdgeOK}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Lab, Complexity.LogProg.Ins}
A predicate on the instructions of a register program with $21$ registers, $2$ oracle deciders
and the codec program's labels for a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$: an equality
test between registers $r$ and $s$ satisfies it exactly when $r\ne s$; an oracle call
satisfies it exactly when its list of argument registers has no repetitions; the three
instructions comparing a register's binary expansion with a payload word of the input never
satisfy it; and every other instruction always satisfies it.
\end{definition}

\lean{Complexity.Codec.edge_gd}
\label{Complexity.Codec.edge_gd}

\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, $y$ a Boolean
word, $B$ a natural number, $\ell$ a label of the $21$-register codec program for $N$, and
$v$ an assignment of naturals to the $21$ registers with $v(r)\le B$ for every $r$. If the
codec program in edge-code mode has at $\ell$ an instruction $I$ such that every equality test
in $I$ compares two distinct registers, every oracle call in $I$ has pairwise distinct argument
registers, and $I$ is not one of the three input-comparison instructions, then the live
configuration at $\ell$ with registers $v$ satisfies the bounded-run guard on input $y$: it
meets the program's syntactic preconditions and all its registers are at most $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The edge-code loop over work tapes]

\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work
tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)$. Let $x,w,r$ be Boolean words,
$y=\langle x,\langle w,r\rangle\rangle$, and $s,B\in\mathbb N$ with $W(2s+1)\le|w|$,
$2|x|+2+2W(2s+1)\le B$ and $s\le B$. For all $m,i\in\mathbb N$ with $i+m+1=k$ and every
assignment $v$ of naturals at most $B$ to the $21$ codec registers with $v(S)=s$, $v(T)=0$,
$v(U)=2|x|+2+2(h_H+3i+2)$ and $v(Q_3)=m+1$: the edge-code mode of the codec program on input
$y$, oracle calls answered by membership in its two decider languages, started at the first
flag-reading label with registers $v$, halts, through configurations meeting the syntactic
preconditions with all registers at most $B$, with answer true exactly when some work tape
$i'$ with $i\le i'<k$ has a $1$ in $w$ at position $h_H+3i'+2$ or at position
$2sW+h_H+3i'+2$ (out-of-range letters read as $0$).
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work
tapes, header width $h_H$ and chunk width $W=W(N)$. Let $x,w,r$ be Boolean words,
$y=\langle x,\langle w,r\rangle\rangle$, $s\in\mathbb N$, $st$ a validity-scan state and $R$
a register record whose $21$ registers are all at most $B_y=(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, with
$R_A=2|x|+2$, $R_S=s$, $R_T=0$, $s\le 2|y|$ and $W(2s+1)\le|w|$. Then the edge-code mode of the
codec program on input $y$, oracle calls answered by membership in its two decider languages,
started at the end-of-scan label with state $st$ and registers $R$, halts through
configurations meeting the syntactic preconditions with all registers at most $B_y$, and its
answer is true exactly when the validator component of $st$ is accepting (the scan found the
word valid and every work tape has a head) and some work tape $i<k$ has a $1$ in $w$ at
position $h_H+3i+2$ or at position $2sW+h_H+3i+2$ (out-of-range letters read as $0$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Edge codes form a logspace language]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.edgeLang_mem}
\label{Complexity.Codec.edgeLang_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.Shape1.eq, Complexity.Codec.edgeChk_def, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang_iff, Complexity.Codec.edge_tail, Complexity.Codec.mem_edgeLang_iff, Complexity.Codec.oneCode_mem, Complexity.Codec.validChk_iff_pre, Complexity.LOGSPACE}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet. The language of
words $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bits}(c),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ such that $c$ is the
radius-$s$ code of a configuration of $N$ on input $x$ that lies in the radius-$s$ window
(every work head within distance $s$ of the origin and every work cell farther out blank) and
has some work head at position $-s$ or $s$ is decidable in logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}
